newsitem.title: USA: US 96/97 corn avg. $2.73, larger '97 acres - FAPRI.
newsitem.headline: US 96/97 corn avg. $2.73, larger '97 acres - FAPRI.

text.p: The 1996 U.S. corn crop will sell for an average $2.73 a bushel and acreage will expand by one million acres in 1997, a think tank said Wednesday.

Food and Agricultural Policy Research Institute at the University of Missouri pegged 1997 corn acreage at 80.6 million acres, compared to 79.6 million planted this year. Corn would retake land lost to soybeans due to rainy spring.
Corn prices will be pressured downward during the winter, a result of the mammoth U.S. crop, FAPRI said, in forecasting a $2.73 a bushel average for the 1996-97 marketing year.
Domestic use would be 6.75 billion bushels, it said.
FAPRI's estimate of domestic use was 110 million bushels higher than the latest Agriculture Department forecast. USDA will update its figures Thursday at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
Lower prices would encourage a rebound in feed usage and ethanol production, the think tank said.
Exports would be lower than 1995-96's 2.2 billion bushels.
FAPRI forecast ending stocks of one billion bushels.
